sections.title: The Covenant Confirmed
observations: In this section, Moses ascends the mountain to receive the law from God. The people are instructed to prepare themselves for this sacred encounter, emphasizing the holiness of God and the seriousness of the covenant they are about to enter into.

Moses reads the Book of the Covenant to the people, and they respond affirmatively, indicating their willingness to obey God's commands. This highlights the importance of community commitment to God's law.

sections.title: Moses and the Elders
observations: Moses takes Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders of Israel with him partway up the mountain. This signifies the importance of leadership and accountability in the community of faith.

They see a manifestation of God's glory, which reinforces the idea that God is both transcendent and immanent. The elders' experience serves as a reminder of the privilege and responsibility of leadership.

sections.title: Moses Receives Instructions
observations: Moses is called further up the mountain to receive the tablets of stone, which contain the law. This signifies the importance of divine revelation and the written word of God in guiding the people.
The instructions given to Moses emphasize the need for obedience and the seriousness of the covenant relationship between God and His people.

importantVerses.commentary: Moses relays the words of the Lord to the people, and they respond, 'All the words which the Lord has said we will do.' This verse highlights the commitment of the people to obey God's commands, which is central to the covenant relationship.
Moses sprinkles the blood on the people, signifying the sealing of the covenant. This act foreshadows the ultimate sacrifice of Christ and the new covenant in His blood.
God instructs Moses to come up to receive the tablets of stone. This emphasizes the importance of God's law and the need for His people to have a written guide for their lives.

questions: What does the act of sprinkling blood on the people signify in the context of the covenant?
How does the experience of the elders seeing God's glory inform our understanding of God's nature?
What implications does the receiving of the law have for the New Testament believer?
